title: Inhibition of lymphocyte homing by carbohydrate-binding proteins, lectins
protocol: Isolate mesenteric lymph nodes and spleen from sacrificed wild-type mice.
Squeeze isolated lymph nodes and spleen between two coverslips to drop lymphocytes into RPMI-1640 medium in a plastic 6-well plate.
Pass the medium through a 70 μm mesh and centrifuge to collect cells.
Incubate collected cells with red blood cell lysis buffer at room temperature for 3 – 5 min.
Add 10 times volume of RPMI-1640 containing 10% fetal bovine serum, incubate the mixture at 37°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,000x g for 5 min and suspend the pellet in 5 ml of RPMI-1640 with 1 μM CMFDA solution, then incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Alternatively, use orange tracker Orange CMRA under the same conditions as CMFDA.
Centrifuge the labeled lymphocytes at 1000 x g for 5 min and suspend in RPMI-1640 containing 10% fetal bovine serum, incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Wash the cell pellet twice with RPMI-1640 and pass through a 70 μm mesh.
Reconstitute cells in 0.9% NaCl to obtain two hundred fifty thousand cells per 100 μl.
Dissolve E-PHA (150 to 400 μg), LEA (150 to 300 μg) or Con A (150 μg) in 150 μl of PBS and intravenously inject through a tail vein.
One hour after the injection, inject CMFDA-labeled lymphocytes (twenty five million cells).
Sacrifice mice one to 24 hours after lymphocyte injection.
Collect peripheral (cervical and lateral axillary) lymph nodes, mesenteric lymph nodes, Peyer's patches, spleen, and thymus from the sacrificed mice.
Squeeze out lymphocytes as described in previous steps.
Remove debris by passing through a 70 μm mesh.
Suspend lymphocytes in 2 ml of PBS.
Analyze cell suspension containing hundred to hundred fifty thousand cells by flow cytometry.
Compare the number of fluorescent cells to the total number of cells.
Conduct control experiments by injecting only PBS.
Compare the ratio of control and lectin-inhibited experiments.
